correctness.rationale: For each distance bound k=2 or 3, any qualifying set has coordinate spans at most k, and every grid geodesic is Manhattan-monotone within its endpoint box. Hence every nonempty set has a unique translated anchored bounding box of dimensions at most 4 by 4, preserving validity. Two distinct executable programs verified all 16-by-2 anchored size histograms exhaustively by iterating every nonempty bitmask and testing shortest routes with monotone BFS and separately enumerated path bitmasks. Each enumeration ran on the actual included files without errors. Each anchored pattern translates to exactly max(m-h+1,0)max(n-w+1,0) placements. Summing the certified histograms proves the boxed coefficients for all m,n>=2, not by extrapolation; no higher-k assertion is made. Explicit 3x3 and 4x4 polynomial checks passed.

value.rationale: The 2024 foundational article explicitly motivates distance-restricted mutual visibility on rectangular grids. The new theorem gives the entire face-size distribution of every feasible set for both k=2 and k=3, not a chosen small-grid number or routine upper bound. Its higher coefficients include a previously known maximum-set layer, but its lower coefficients supply independent new cardinality information that cannot be recovered from the optimum alone. Exact all-size counts are useful for enumerating placements under restricted geodesic reachability, random selection models, and studying the associated downward-closed visibility complex. The theorem applies to an infinite two-parameter family because the locality reduction is structural; the finite enumeration is complete and small. No general k>3 theorem or practical performance gain is asserted.
